mainTopic: Why a סוכה above twenty אמה is פסולה: the wording of the משנה compared with מבוי, and three sources for the height limit
overview: The משנה lists four ways a סוכה can be פסולה: higher than twenty אמה (רבי יהודה disagrees), lower than ten טפחים, missing walls, or more sun than shade. The גמרא compares this to a משנה in מסכת עירובין about a מבוי higher than twenty אמה, where the משנה gives a fix: lower it. It asks why our משנה just says 'פסולה', and gives two answers: סוכה is a Torah law while מבוי is rabbinic, or a סוכה has too many rules to list all the fixes. Then the גמרא asks for the source of the twenty-אמה limit and brings three answers. רבה says a person must know he is in a סוכה, and above twenty אמה the eye does not notice the roof. רבי זירא says the roof must give the shade, and above twenty אמה the walls give the shade instead. רבא says a סוכה must be a temporary home, and above twenty אמה a building must be permanent. אביי challenges רבי זירא and רבא, and each one defends his reason.

steps.title: A סוכה taller than twenty אמה is unfit
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a סוכה higher than twenty אמה is פסולה, and רבי יהודה disagrees and says it is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A סוכה that is taller than twenty אמה is not kosher. רבי יהודה says it is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens the מסכת with its first rule: a סוכה has a maximum height. רבי יהודה argues and allows a taller one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The height is measured up to the roof covering, the סכך. The first opinion sets a ceiling of twenty אמה, and anything above it is פסולה. רבי יהודה rules that a סוכה higher than twenty אמה is still כשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: A booth with a roof of branches or leaves, used on the holiday of סוכות
A cubit, a measure of length of about half a meter
Unfit, not kosher for the מצוה

phrases.english: A sukkah that is high
above twenty cubits is unfit.
And Rabbi Yehuda deems it fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: סוּכָּה שֶׁהִיא גְּבוֹהָה לְמַעְלָה מֵעֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סוכה higher than twenty אמה is פסולה; רבי יהודה rules it כשרה.

steps.title: Three more ways a סוכה is unfit
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds three more problems that make a סוכה פסולה: lower than ten טפחים, missing walls, or more sun than shade.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also unfit: a סוכה that is not even ten טפחים tall, one that does not have three walls, and one where the sunlight coming through is more than the shade.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps listing what makes a סוכה פסולה. Here it gives a minimum height, a wall requirement, and a shade requirement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 gave a maximum height; this step gives the minimum of ten טפחים. It also requires walls and says the סכך must give more shade than sun. No one argues on these three rules in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Handbreadths, a small measure of length
Its sunlight is more than its shade

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה lists four ways a סוכה is פסולה: too tall (over twenty אמה), too short (under ten טפחים), not enough walls, and more sun than shade.

phrases.english: And one that is not ten handbreadths high,
and one that does not have (three) walls,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word 'three' in the round brackets and some leave it out.

phrases.english: and one whose sunlight is greater than its shade, is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of things that make a סוכה פסולה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סוכה under ten טפחים, without enough walls, or with more sun than shade is פסולה.

steps.title: A similar mishnah about an alleyway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from מסכת עירובין: a מבוי higher than twenty אמה must be lowered, and רבי יהודה says this is not needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in another משנה: if a מבוי is higher than twenty אמה, one must lower it. רבי יהודה says he does not need to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a parallel משנה about a מבוי that has the same twenty-אמה limit. This is a setup for the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cases match: same limit of twenty אמה, and רבי יהודה disagrees in both. But the wording is different. For a מבוי the משנה gives a fix (lower it), while for a סוכה it just says פסולה.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
An alleyway; a beam across its entrance lets people carry inside it on שבת
He should reduce it, meaning lower the height

phrases.english: GEMARA: We learned there:
phrases.notes: 'There' means a משנה in מסכת עירובין.

phrases.aramaic: מָבוֹי שֶׁהוּא גָּבוֹהַּ מֵעֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה — יְמַעֵט.
phrases.english: An alleyway that is higher than twenty cubits, one must lower it.
phrases.notes: The height is the beam placed across the entrance to the alleyway.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: He does not need to.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel source to compare with the first ruling of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מבוי higher than twenty אמה must be lowered; רבי יהודה says this is not needed.

steps.title: Why one mishnah says unfit and the other gives a fix
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the סוכה משנה says 'פסולה' while the מבוי משנה gives a fix.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the משנה about a סוכה say 'it is unfit', while the משנה about a מבוי teaches how to fix it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the two משניות use different wording for the same kind of rule, and asks why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases have a twenty-אמה limit, so we would expect the same wording. The question is about wording: why not tell us how to fix the סוכה too? The next step answers this, and step 6 gives a second answer.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Used to ask why two similar cases are treated differently
A fix, a way to correct the problem

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not asking whether the twenty-אמה rule is true. It only asks why the two משניות use different wording.

phrases.english: What is different regarding a sukkah
that it teaches 'unfit,'
and what is different regarding an alleyway
that it teaches a fix?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא גַּבֵּי סוּכָּה דְּתָנֵי פְּסוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the wording of the two משניות quoted in steps 1 and 3
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the סוכה משנה says 'פסולה' while the מבוי משנה tells you how to fix it

steps.title: Torah law versus rabbinic law
steps.stepSummary: Because סוכה is a Torah law, the משנה rules it פסולה. Because מבוי is a rabbinic law, the משנה teaches a fix.
steps.simpleTranslation: A סוכה is from the Torah, so the משנה teaches that it is unfit. A מבוי is from the Rabbis, so the משנה teaches how to fix it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 4 about why the two משניות use different wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a Torah מצוה like סוכה, the main point is whether the מצוה counts at all, so the משנה says 'פסולה'. With a rabbinic rule like מבוי, the משנה can simply tell you how to fix the problem. The difference in wording comes from the difference in the level of the law.

phrases.english: Sukka, which is from the Torah,
it teaches: unfit.
An alleyway, which is rabbinic,
phrases.notes: The need to fix a מבוי so you can carry there is a rule of the Rabbis.

phrases.english: it teaches the fix.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question raised in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה in סוכה says 'פסולה' while the משנה in עירובין gives a fix.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The wording depends on the level of the law: Torah law gets 'פסולה', rabbinic law gets a fix.

steps.title: Many rules versus few rules
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: even a Torah law could have been taught as a fix. But סוכה has so many rules that the משנה simply calls it פסולה, while מבוי has few rules, so a fix is given.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer, say this: even for Torah laws the משנה could teach a fix. But a סוכה has many details, so the משנה just says plainly that it is unfit. A מבוי does not have many details, so the משנה teaches the fix.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second, different answer to the same question from step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer drops the Torah-versus-rabbinic idea. The issue is practical: lowering a סוכה is not enough, because it must also meet many other rules (walls, shade, size). Explaining all those fixes would take too long. A מבוי becomes fine once it is lowered, so a short fix works.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces another answer)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a rejection of the first answer. It is a second option, and both remain possible.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
even with Torah laws it would teach a fix,
however, sukka, whose details are many,
it states plainly and teaches: unfit.
An alleyway, whose details are not many,
it teaches the fix.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the same question that step 5 answered.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the two משניות use different wording.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A סוכה has too many rules to list fixes for, so the משנה simply says 'פסולה'. A מבוי has few rules, so a fix is given.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two reasons for the wording difference: (1) Torah law versus rabbinic law, or (2) a סוכה has many rules while a מבוי has few.

steps.title: Where does the twenty-אמה rule come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves from the wording to the law itself and asks for the source of the twenty-אמה limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move: it asks for the source of the rule that a סוכה above twenty אמה is פסולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was only about the wording of the משנה. Now the גמרא wants to know where the rule itself comes from. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: From where are these matters?
phrases.notes: He means the rule that a סוכה higher than twenty אמה is פסולה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the wording question and opens a new question about the source of the law in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the twenty-אמה height limit of a סוכה.

steps.title: רבה derives the rule from 'so that your generations will know'
steps.stepSummary: רבה derives the twenty-אמה limit from a פסוק: the מצוה requires a person to know he is in a סוכה. Above twenty אמה, the eye does not notice the roof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: the פסוק says, 'So that your generations will know that I made the Children of Israel live in סוכות.' Up to twenty אמה, a person knows he is living in a סוכה. Above twenty אמה, a person does not know he is living in a סוכה, because his eye does not catch sight of the roof.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the question from step 7 by showing that a פסוק is the source for the twenty-אמה limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the purpose of the סוכה is that people should 'know' they are sitting in one. A person notices a roof (סכך) that is twenty אמה high or lower without trying. When the roof is higher than that, it is out of his natural line of sight, so the purpose of the מצוה is lost.

keyTerms.meaning: The eye catches sight of it

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה, a סוכה must let a person notice that he is in a סוכה. Above twenty אמה, the eye does not see the roof, so the סוכה is פסולה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the first of three different sources the גמרא gives for the twenty-אמה limit. רבה ties it to awareness: the eye must notice the roof.

phrases.english: Rabba said: because the verse says:
"So that your generations will know

phrases.aramaic: כִּי בַסּוּכּוֹת הוֹשַׁבְתִּי אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״,
phrases.english: that I made the Children of Israel live in sukkot,"
up to twenty cubits,
a person knows that he lives in a sukka;
above twenty cubits,
a person does not know that he lives in a sukka,
because the eye does not catch sight of it.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the roof of the סוכה, which is too high to notice without trying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question asked in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the twenty-אמה limit.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'למען ידעו דורותיכם' requires awareness of the סוכה, and above twenty אמה the eye does not see the roof.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סוכה above twenty אמה is פסולה because its roof is out of natural sight, so a person is not aware he is in a סוכה.

steps.title: רבי זירא's source: the סוכה must give shade
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא offers a different source for the twenty-אמה limit. A סוכה is meant to give shade, and above twenty אמה the shade comes from the walls, not from the roof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: we learn it from here: "And there shall be a סוכה for shade by day from the heat." Up to twenty אמה, a person sits in the shade of the סוכה. Above twenty אמה, a person does not sit in the shade of the סוכה, but in the shade of the walls.
steps.whatsHappening: After רבה's answer, the גמרא brings a second answer from רבי זירא for where the twenty-אמה limit comes from. He uses a different פסוק, one about shade.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says a סוכה is for shade, so the shade must come from the סוכה's roof. When the roof is very high, the tall walls block the sun on their own. The person is then shaded by the walls, not by the roof, so it does not count as a סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: From here, meaning "this is my source"

steps.confusionAlert: "The shade of the סוכה" here means the shade made by the roof covering, not shade from anywhere inside the סוכה. That is why shade from the walls does not count.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: from here
"And there shall be a sukkah for shade by day from the heat"
Up to twenty amos
a person sits in the shade of the sukkah,
above twenty amos
a person does not sit in the shade of the sukkah
but rather in the shade of the walls.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different answer to the question in Step 7, alongside רבה's answer in Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The twenty-אמה limit comes from the פסוק calling a סוכה a source of shade. Above twenty אמה, the shade comes from the walls, not from the roof.

steps.title: אביי's challenge: a סוכה in a shady valley
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבי זירא. If the shade must come from the roof, a סוכה built in עשתרות קרנים, where mountains already block the sun, should not be kosher either.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But if so, someone who builds his סוכה in עשתרות קרנים, would that also not be a סוכה?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבי זירא's reasoning by showing it seems to lead to a strange result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In עשתרות קרנים, the mountains already shade the area, so the roof does not actually create the shade. By רבי זירא's logic, that סוכה should not count. Since it is obvious that such a סוכה is kosher, his reasoning looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so: a phrase that pushes an idea to an unwanted result
A place surrounded by mountains that block the sun
So too? (Would that also be the case?)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But if so,
one who makes his sukkah in Ashteros Karnayim,
phrases.notes: A place between mountains whose shadow blocks the sun, so the roof is not what gives the shade.

phrases.english: would it also not be a sukkah?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי זירא's shade-based reasoning from Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's claim that a סוכה is not kosher if its shade does not come from the roof
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In a naturally shaded place, the roof does not create the shade either, yet such a סוכה is surely kosher.

steps.title: רבי זירא answers: imagine taking the outside shade away
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains the difference. Remove the mountains, and the roof still gives shade. Remove the walls of a tall סוכה, and the roof gives no real shade.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, if you take away עשתרות קרנים, there is still shade from the סוכה. Here, if you take away the walls, there is no shade from the סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא defends his source by showing the two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is: "Take away the other thing. Does the roof still give shade?" In the valley, the mountains are outside the סוכה, and without them the roof still works. In a too-tall סוכה, the roof is so high that without the walls the sun would get in underneath, so the roof itself is not doing its job.

phrases.english: He said to him:
There, remove Ashteros Karnayim
and there is shade of the sukkah.
Here, remove the walls
and there is no shade of the sukkah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָתָם, דַּל עַשְׁתְּרוֹת קַרְנַיִם
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any time the roof is not the actual source of shade, the סוכה would be invalid.
steps.terutzMaskana: What matters is whether the roof would give shade without the outside factor. Mountains are outside the סוכה, but the walls are part of it, so a too-tall roof truly fails.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא's test: picture the outside shade-maker gone. If the roof would still give shade, the סוכה is kosher.

steps.title: רבא's source: a סוכה must be a temporary home
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a third source. The Torah says to leave your permanent home for a temporary one for seven days. Above twenty אמה, a building has to be built as a permanent structure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: we learn it from here: "In סוכות you shall live for seven days." The Torah said: for all seven days, leave your permanent home and live in a temporary home. Up to twenty אמה, a person can make his home a temporary home. Above twenty אמה, a person cannot make his home a temporary home, only a permanent one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third answer, from רבא, for where the twenty-אמה limit comes from. It is based on the idea that a סוכה is a temporary home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah wants us to move out of our sturdy home into a temporary one. A low structure can be built flimsy and temporary. Anything taller than twenty אמה must be built strong and permanent to stand, so it no longer fits the idea of a סוכה.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three sources for the twenty-אמה limit: רבה (you must know you are in a סוכה), רבי זירא (shade from the roof), and רבא (a temporary home).
steps.whyThisMatters: רבא's idea of a סוכה as a temporary home becomes a key theme for understanding many סוכה laws.

phrases.english: And Rava said: from here
"In sukkos you shall dwell seven days."
The Torah said:
for all seven days
leave your permanent home
and dwell in a temporary home.
Up to twenty amos
a person makes his home a temporary home,
above twenty amos

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אָדָם עוֹשֶׂה דִּירָתוֹ דִּירַת עֲרַאי
phrases.english: a person does not make his home a temporary home
but rather a permanent home.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third, different answer to the question in Step 7, after רבה and רבי זירא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The twenty-אמה limit comes from the requirement that a סוכה be a temporary home. Above twenty אמה, a building must be permanent.

steps.title: Iron walls should make a סוכה invalid
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבא: if a סוכה must be a דירת עראי, then a סוכה with iron walls should not be kosher, and that is clearly wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, if someone made iron walls and put סכך on top of them, would you also say it is not a סוכה?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's reason from Step 12. He says it leads to a result nobody accepts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said a סוכה must be a temporary home. Iron walls make a very permanent structure. By רבא's logic, a סוכה with iron walls should be invalid, but everyone agrees such a סוכה is kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: "But if so, now..." A phrase that opens a challenge by showing where an idea leads
He placed the סכך (the roof covering)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: He is speaking to רבא, who just gave the temporary-home reason in the last step.

phrases.english: But if that is so,
if he made walls of iron
and put the roofing on top of them,
would you also say it is not a sukkah?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's source from Step 12 by showing it leads to an unacceptable result.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reason that a סוכה must be a דירת עראי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a סוכה must be temporary, a permanent iron-walled סוכה should be invalid. But it is kosher, so the reason seems wrong.

steps.title: The height decides, not the strength of the walls
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that his rule depends on height. Up to twenty אמה, people build temporary homes, so even a permanent-style סוכה is kosher. Above twenty אמה, people must build permanently, so even a flimsy סוכה is not kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what I am telling you. Up to twenty אמה, where a person makes his home a temporary home, even when he builds it as a permanent home, he still fulfills the מצוה. Above twenty אמה, where a person makes his home a permanent home, even when he builds it as a temporary home, he does not fulfill the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers אביי by explaining what he really meant. The question is what kind of building that height normally requires, not how strong this particular סוכה is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Below twenty אמה, a temporary structure can stand, so the height counts as a "temporary-home height." That stays true even if one chooses iron walls. Above twenty אמה, a structure must be built strongly to stand, so the height counts as "permanent," even if one builds it flimsily.

keyTerms.meaning: "This is what I am telling you." Used to clarify what one really meant

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, the twenty-אמה limit is about height type. A low סוכה is kosher even if built strongly. A סוכה above twenty אמה is not kosher even if built weakly.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבא requires every סוכה to be physically flimsy. He only means the height must be one where a temporary home is normal. Strong walls below twenty אמה are fine.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רבא's rule judges a type of structure by its height, not by the materials the builder happened to use.

phrases.english: He said to him: This is what I am saying to you:
Up to twenty cubits,
where a person makes his dwelling a temporary dwelling,
when he makes it a permanent dwelling,
he also fulfills his obligation.
Above twenty cubits,
where a person makes his dwelling a permanent dwelling,
when he makes it a temporary dwelling,
he also does not fulfill his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from Step 13 by clarifying רבא's rule from Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarification of the original statement: the rule depends on height category, not on actual construction.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי understood רבא to mean that each סוכה must actually be built flimsily, so an iron-walled סוכה would be invalid.
steps.terutzMaskana: The test is the height. Up to twenty אמה, any construction is fine. Above twenty אמה, no construction helps.
